cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are changed by heat and/or pressure without melting

cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Regional metamorphism: large-scale, caused by tectonic compression and heat during mountain building; produces foliated rocks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Contact metamorphism: local, caused by heat from an igneous intrusion; produces non-foliated rocks

cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Foliation: alignment of minerals in bands, produced by directed pressure (e.g. slate to schist to gneiss with increasing grade)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Index minerals indicate metamorphic grade: chlorite (low), biotite, garnet, staurolite, kyanite, sillimanite (high)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Metamorphic Rocks
cards.back: Common metamorphic rocks: slate (from mudstone), schist (from shale), gneiss (from granite), marble (from limestone), quartzite (from sandstone)

cards.back: 1. For Metamorphic Rocks questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3.
